messages:
jia-chen: FYI saw a cluster of OOMs after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout (latency-optimized kernels). P95 steady but OOM rate up ~2.4x on kv-cache heavy workloads.
jia-chen: Root cause guess: different kernel codepaths allocate larger temporary workspaces + more fragmented free lists so PyTorch allocator fails to coalesce. Quick dump below.
jia-chen: ```
Cmd: python -m runtime.bench --model t5-enc-dec --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kv-cache
Torch mem summary (snippet):
Allocated: 24.9 GB, Cached: 6.2 GB, Active allocs: 312
Free segments: 512 entries, avg size 12 MB, holes: sawtooth pattern after long-run
OOM stack: aten::empty -> CUDACachingAllocator::raw_alloc -> attempt_expandable_segments
```
infra-bot: jenkins/job/rt-kernel-rollout #452 failed  -> https://ci.redwood/rt-kernel-rollout/452/logs (auto-attached logs) :warning:
infra-bot: Recent change: kernel_selector v2 enabled small-block tiling for heads which increases workspace per-kernel by ~1.2x in worst case.
dmitri: Thanks for the dump. Two quick knobs to try: set `max_split_size_mb` lower so allocator avoids large splits, and tweak `expandable_segments` to prefer larger segment reuse.
dmitri: e.g., try: `expandable_segments=true`, `max_split_size_mb=64`, `garbage_collection_threshold=0.6` — in our last incident that reduced fragmentation on long-lived kv-cache by ~30%.
marta: We did a micro-experiment last month where we implemented transient buffer reuse for attention workspaces (reuse preallocated pool keyed by sequence-length bucket). Patch lowered peak by ~1.8GB for seq 2048 on 8 batch. I can dig up the patch.
marta: Patch snippet:```cpp
// preallocate buckets by seq_len/256
BufferPool::get(bucket_id) { if (!empty) return pop(); else return cudaMalloc(size); }
// on kernel exit: BufferPool::put(buf);
```
sam: Can we get the profiler flamegraph for a warm run vs cold run? Want to see which ops balloon workspace. Also confirm if kernel selector changed the kernel for multihead matmul.
sylvia: Attached perf trace (filtered):
```
Time(ms) | op_name | workspace_mb
2200 | attention_fwd_tiled_v2 | 512
2210 | matmul_kv | 128
2215 | attention_fwd_tiled_v1 | 320
```
sylvia: Notice attention_fwd_tiled_v2 is the new one and uses larger transient workspace.
dmitri: Another knob: `garbage_collection_threshold` helps for long-running processes where fragmentation accumulates. Setting to 0.5 triggers earlier GC and frees cached blocks back to driver. But tradeoff is more cudaFree/alloc churn.
dmitri: Also consider `max_split_size_mb=0` (disable splitting) for allocator builds that suffer fragmentation from many mid-size frees — sometimes prevents sawtooth of small holes. Experiment both.
jia-chen: Good suggestions. I'll canary two configs on staging: A) expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=128, gc_threshold=0.7 (favor bigger segments) B) expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=64, gc_threshold=0.55 (favor reuse + earlier GC).
jia-chen: Plan: run 6h steady-schedule with kv-cache churn and measure OOM count, peak allocated, cached size, and free-seg histogram.
infra-bot: Started job rt-canary/179812-oncall with configs A and B. Logs will appear in ~30m.
marta: If B looks promising we should land lightweight BufferPool reuse (non-invasive) into runtime: small change, adds a few hundred bytes per bucket. Will prepare PR and attach perf numbers.
sam: Also add a small metric: `allocator.free_fragmentation_ratio` (free_bytes / total_pool_bytes) so we can alert if it drifts.
sylvia: Onboarding note: if someone reproduces locally, run `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.55,max_split_size_mb:64` and warm with a few iterations before collecting the trace.
dmitri: One more: watch for KV-cache eviction patterns — when we evict a big chunk it creates many free segments. If allocator split policy creates many small free segments, fragmentation explodes. Consider coalescing on free path as well.
jia-chen: Thanks all — will post results. If B reduces OOMs we'll keep and then iterate on BufferPool. :thumbsup:
